intro_html: Buffalo wings without the wing prices, and a whole lot more protein per bite. This skillet packs 44 grams of protein into a bowl that lands at about $3.95 (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings out of one pan means lunch is handled for the better part of two weeks.
cost_closing_html: About $3.95 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 bowls delivers 44 grams of protein and 661 calories, so it eats like a real meal, not a snack.
upsell_html: Big flavor, small price, and two weeks of lunches ready to grab. That is a win any way you count it. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Buy the store-brand frozen fries. At around $2.48 a bag they cook up the same as the name brand and save you real money across four bags.
One bottle of buffalo sauce covers the whole batch, so skip the fancy small-batch stuff and grab the standard wing sauce.
Fat-free cheddar melts fine on hot food, so use it here and save the block cheese for another recipe.
make_it: Brown 6 pounds of 93/7 ground turkey with a chopped yellow onion until no pink is left.
Bake the fries on sheet pans while the turkey cooks so nothing sits waiting.
Stir the buffalo wing sauce and shredded carrots into the turkey and let it simmer a few minutes.
Pile the buffalo turkey over the fries in each container.
Sprinkle the fat-free cheddar on top while everything is hot so it melts in.
